In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of partnership agreements on the nature of the employment relationship and, in particular, the extent to which they have the effect of reducing union influence and effectiveness.
the role of trade unions in the workplace and the way in which trade unions are changing their approach in order to adapt to new economic and social conditions.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the partnership agreements were not successful in terms of union influence.
the partnership consultation process in both firms was not effective.
the partnership approach to consultation is a double-edged sword.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
partnership is an effective tool for employers to dominate unions, provided that employers are dominant and unions are weak.
the effectiveness of consultation is dependent on the context of the industrial relations climate and history of management-union relations.
partnership agreements can be a useful vehicle for improving the effectiveness of union influence in some circumstances.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the impact of employer dominance on consultation under partnership agreements is not inevitable.
consultation can be a vehicle for union voice and influence in employer dominant firms, but that this is not inevitable.
partnership agreements can enable unions to maintain their influence, even when they are not the dominant partner in the agreement.
